name: CRSOM
desc: A project for BZU event CRSOM with complex forms and relaible delivery.
challenge: Meridian's ops teams were drowning in spreadsheets. Decisions were being made on data that was 4+ hours old — a lifetime in logistics. When a truck breaks down or a route needs rerouting, you need to know now, not after a refresh cycle.
approach: I rebuilt the data pipeline to push via WebSockets instead of polling, and redesigned the dashboard around the concept of alert-first: the system surfaces what needs attention before you think to look for it. D3 handles the heavy visualization; a custom Rust API handles stream aggregation at scale.

process.title: Discovery
process.desc: Spent two weeks shadowing ops managers across three shifts. Mapped every moment where a decision had to be made and what data was (not) available.

process.title: Redesign
process.desc: Rebuilt the information hierarchy around urgency, not recency. Introduced a triage panel that separates alerts from trends from history.

process.title: Ship
process.desc: Three months of weekly cycles. Feature flags let us test with a pilot cohort of 12 teams before rolling out to all 200+.

outcome: Meridian's platform is now the centrepiece of their enterprise sales pitch. Decision latency dropped from hours to under 60 seconds. The dashboard architecture became the template for every feature they shipped the following year.
